chunks: And from him, from Humayd, from al-Hasan ibn Sam'ah, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abd al-Ghaffar al-Ta'i, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who had two sisters (concubines) under his ownership, and he had intercourse with one of them, then intended to have intercourse with the other, he said: 'He must free the first one from his ownership.' I asked: 'To whom?' He said: 'To some of his family.' I asked: 'And if he was unaware of this until he had intercourse with the second one?' He said: 'Both become forbidden to him.'

His saying (peace be upon him): 'Both become forbidden to him' means this as long as both remain in his ownership. As for when the ownership of one of them is removed, then the other has become permissible to him. And we have previously presented what indicates this, and what increases its clarification is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man has intercourse with two sisters who are both his concubines?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of 'two sisters' (أختان) specifically within the context of concubinage (milk al-yamin), distinguishing it from the general marital prohibition. The scholar notes that the permanent prohibition (haraman) applies only while both sisters remain in his ownership; once one is freed, the other becomes permissible again, a nuance derived from the specific wording of the Imam. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the condition of simultaneous ownership in determining the scope of the prohibition.
